purpose: Perform the disjoint even-parity Fourier sums from v1.0 symbolically before determinant expansion. This removes the explicit 2^(q-n) character enumeration exactly and isolates the remaining obstruction as a top exterior coefficient of one rank-2 local tensor per original Boolean variable.

generic_exterior_lemma.setup: Let G={1,...,d}. For row vectors a_j,b_j over characteristic zero and t_j in {+1,-1}, define r_j(t_j)=a_j+t_j b_j. Let E_G={t: product_j t_j=1}.
generic_exterior_lemma.identity: sum_{t in E_G} wedge_{j=1}^d (a_j+t_j b_j) = 2^(d-1) * (wedge_j a_j + wedge_j b_j), with the d=1 case interpreted directly as a_1+b_1.
proof: Expand the wedge product by a subset S of positions choosing b_j instead of a_j.
The coefficient of that mixed wedge term is sum_{t in E_G} product_{j in S} t_j.
E_G is the even-parity subgroup of {+1,-1}^d. Its character annihilator consists only of the empty character and the full-set character.
Therefore every proper nonempty mixed subset cancels, while S=empty and S=G each contribute |E_G|=2^(d-1).

specialization_to_v1_0.augmented_matrix: For fixed sign vector t, Dhat_F(t)=det([[M0,U],[-T V^T,I+T]]). Let q be the number of occurrences and N=3m+q.
specialization_to_v1_0.fixed_top_rows: Let R_fixed be the ordered wedge of the 3m rows of [M0,U].
specialization_to_v1_0.bottom_row_split: Bottom occurrence row o is a_o+t_o b_o with a_o=(0,e_o) and b_o=(-v_o,e_o), where v_o is the occurrence row of V.
specialization_to_v1_0.groups: For original Boolean variable i with occurrence set G_i define A_i=wedge_{o in G_i} a_o and B_i=wedge_{o in G_i} b_o, using a fixed within-group occurrence order.
specialization_to_v1_0.orientation_sign: Let epsilon_F be the sign of the permutation taking the original bottom-row occurrence order to the concatenation G_1,G_2,... in the chosen variable order.
specialization_to_v1_0.scaling_cancellation: The local factors multiply to product_i 2^(|G_i|-1)=2^(q-n) for nonempty variable groups. This cancels exactly against the v1.0 prefactor 2^(n-q) in #SAT(F)=2^(n-q) sum_{s in E} Dhat_F(s). Degree-1 groups contribute factor one and the same formula remains valid.

bounded_occurrence_consequence.degree2: A_i+B_i is a sum of two decomposable bivectors.
bounded_occurrence_consequence.degree3: A_i+B_i is a sum of two decomposable trivectors; this is the exterior form of the same 2-vs-1 Boolean switch isolated by v1.4/v2.4.
bounded_occurrence_consequence.polynomial_description: All a_o,b_o and all local exterior factors have O(1) degree under the bounded-occurrence normalization, so the expression has polynomial syntactic size. No Fourier character is enumerated in the representation.

what_is_and_is_not_solved.solved: The exponential parity-subspace SUM itself is removed from the representation: its action is exactly the local all-a versus all-b projector above.
what_is_and_is_not_solved.remaining: Computing the top coefficient of the product of n rank-2 exterior tensors without expanding their 2^n choices is not proved polynomial. A naive exterior-basis representation has dimension exponential in q and is forbidden.
what_is_and_is_not_solved.interpretation: The remaining hard object is no longer a generic Fourier sum. It is a source-aligned contraction of secant-Grassmann tensors of degree at most three with the frozen fixed top wedge.
